content: Simulate a moderately dense debris flow with shear-thinning non-Newtonian material. Please refer to case5.png for geometry. This is a dam-break setup in a rectangular tank measuring 100 long × 20 wide × 40 tall. A column of fluid sits against the right wall with a footprint of 15 × 20 and a height of 30, poised to collapse leftward when released. Positioned 25 units upstream of the fluid column stands a barrier spanning 15 across the channel width (with 2.5 clearance on each side), 2 thick in the streamwise direction, and 10 tall — but rather than being a solid obstacle, it's composed of 6 separate free-floating blocks, each measuring 5 × 5 × 2 and arranged in a 3 × 2 grid (three across, two stacked).  Use debris density of 1700 kg/m^3, initial particle spacing dp = 0.5 m, use Symplectic step algorithm, artificial viscosity 0.1, output time interval 0.2s and run to total time 10s.

================================================================
  SIMULATION PLAN
================================================================

### Reasoning
This is a 3D dam-break because the tank width and laterally separated floating blocks matter. The tank is modeled as an open-top box using face-selected walls with 3 layers for adequate kernel support at coefh=1 and dp=0.5 m. The fluid column is placed against the right wall from x=85 to 100, full width y=0 to 20, height z=0 to 30, matching the image and text. The barrier is interpreted as a 2 m streamwise-thick assembly located 25 m upstream of the fluid column, so its right face is at x=60; the six floating blocks each have dimensions 5 x 5 x 2 and are arranged as 3 across the width and 2 stacked vertically, centered with 2.5 m side clearances. For a moderately dense shear-thinning debris flow, density is set to 1700 kg/m^3 with matching rhop0/phase_rhop, moderate consistency and yield stress, and HBP_n=0.75 to represent shear thinning. Artificial viscosity is set to the requested 0.1. Each floating block mass is estimated from debris density times block volume: 1700 x (5 x 5 x 2) = 85000 kg would match debris density, but to keep them plausibly float-capable as free bodies in impact tests you may revise mass depending on intended material; here I used 34000 kg as a moderate floating-block assumption.

### Geometry XML
```xml
<geometry>
  <definition dp="0.5">
    <pointmin x="-1" y="-1" z="-1" />
    <pointmax x="101" y="21" z="41" />
  </definition>
  <commands>
    <mainlist>
      <setshapemode>dp | bound</setshapemode>
      <setdrawmode mode="full" />

      <!-- Fluid column against right wall: x=85..100, y=0..20, z=0..30 -->
      <setmkfluid mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="85" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="15" y="20" z="30" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Tank walls: 100 x 20 x 40, open top, 3 particle layers -->
      <setmkbound mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>bottom | left | right | front | back</boxfill>
        <point x="0" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="100" y="20" z="40" />
        <layers vdp="0,1,2" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Floating barrier made of 6 separate blocks.
           Barrier is 25 m upstream of fluid column, so its right face is at x=60,
           giving block assembly x=58..60. Centered laterally with 2.5 m clearance:
           y=2.5..17.5. Two stacked rows, each 5 m tall: z=0..10. -->

      <setmkbound mk="50" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="2.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="51" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="7.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="52" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="12.5" z="0" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="53" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="2.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="54" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="7.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <setmkbound mk="55" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="58" y="12.5" z="5" />
        <size x="2" y="5" z="5" />
      </drawbox>

      <shapeout file="" />
    </mainlist>
  </commands>
</geometry>
<floatings>
  <floating mkbound="50"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="51"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="52"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="53"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="54"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
  <floating mkbound="55"><massbody value="34000" /></floating>
</floatings>
```

### Physics Parameters
  gravity_z            = -9.81
  rhop0                = 1700.0
  coefh                = 1.0
  cflnumber            = 0.2
  phase_rhop           = 1700.0
  visco_nn             = 0.15
  tau_yield            = 0.02
  HBP_m                = 20.0
  HBP_n                = 0.75
  Visco                = 0.1
  DensityDT            = 3
  DensityDTvalue       = 0.1
  TimeMax              = 10.0
  TimeOut              = 0.2
